database_summary: Operational retail/brewery dataset with product/catalog dimensions, inventory and purchasing events, customer orders and simple web analytics. Mix of slowly changing descriptive tables (products, product_groups, packaging, breweries), event/history tables (purchases, monthly_sales, ticker, web_counter_hist, web_page_visits, server_heartbeat, picking_log, emp_hire_periods) and current-state snapshot tables (inventory, product_alcohol, product_minimums, monthly_budget). Many lookup/dimension tables are small. Several tables use composite natural keys (month/day + product or app/page).

accepted.name: product_monthly_sales
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_id,
  mth,
  SUM(qty) AS qty
FROM monthly_sales
GROUP BY product_id, mth
accepted.description: Aggregated monthly sales per product. Use this when you need total quantity sold by product and month (time series, budgeting comparisons, trend analysis). | Use for: monthly sales trends for a product; compare actual sales to budget by month; time series joins to product attributes

accepted.name: product_total_sales
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_id,
  SUM(qty) AS qty_total
FROM monthly_sales
GROUP BY product_id
accepted.description: Total sales quantity per product across all months. Useful for ranking top-selling products, computing lifetime sales, or joining to product metadata. | Use for: top N products by sales; product-level lifetime sales for reporting; join lifetime sales to product groups or alcohol properties

accepted.name: products_with_group
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.id AS id,
  p.name AS name,
  p.group_id AS group_id,
  pg.name AS name__group
FROM products p
LEFT JOIN product_groups pg ON p.group_id = pg.id
accepted.description: Denormalized product rows with their product group name. Use when you need product attributes together with group metadata for reporting or joins. | Use for: list products with their group names; aggregate sales by product group by joining to this CTE; filter products by group attributes

accepted.name: products_with_alcohol
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.id AS id,
  p.name AS name,
  p.group_id AS group_id,
  pa.sales_volume AS sales_volume,
  pa.abv AS abv
FROM products p
LEFT JOIN product_alcohol pa ON p.id = pa.product_id
accepted.description: Products joined to alcohol properties (sales_volume, abv). Useful for analyses that need alcohol attributes next to product identifiers. | Use for: compare sales by ABV; filter products by alcohol strength; enrich sales/inventory with ABV for reporting

accepted.name: orders_with_lines
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ol.id AS id,
  ol.order_id AS order_id,
  ol.product_id AS product_id,
  ol.qty AS qty,
  ol.amount AS amount,
  o.customer_id AS customer_id,
  o.ordered AS ordered,
  o.delivery AS delivery
FROM orderlines ol
LEFT JOIN orders o ON ol.order_id = o.id
accepted.description: Order lines joined to their parent orders and customers. One row per orderline with order-level context (ordered date, customer). Useful for revenue, fulfillment, and customer purchase history queries. | Use for: customer purchase history; order line level revenue/time analysis; fulfillment and delivery timing queries

accepted.name: inventory_with_locations
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  i.id AS id,
  i.location_id AS location_id,
  i.product_id AS product_id,
  i.purchase_id AS purchase_id,
  i.qty AS qty,
  l.warehouse AS warehouse,
  l.aisle AS aisle,
  l.position AS position
FROM inventory i
LEFT JOIN locations l ON i.location_id = l.id
accepted.description: Inventory rows enriched with location attributes (warehouse, aisle, position). Use for stock location reporting, picking optimizations, and spatial inventory analyses. | Use for: where is stock located for a product; aggregate inventory by warehouse/aisle; optimize picking by location

accepted.name: purchases_enriched
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.id AS id,
  p.purchased AS purchased,
  p.brewery_id AS brewery_id,
  p.product_id AS product_id,
  p.qty AS qty,
  p.cost AS cost,
  b.name AS name__brewery,
  pr.name AS name__product
FROM purchases p
LEFT JOIN breweries b ON p.brewery_id = b.id
LEFT JOIN products pr ON p.product_id = pr.id
accepted.description: Purchases with brewery and product metadata (product name, brewery name). Useful for supplier spend analysis and product-level costing. | Use for: supplier costing over time; purchase quantities by product; join purchases to sales for margin analysis

accepted.name: web_daily_devices
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  day,
  pc,
  tablet,
  phone,
  (COALESCE(pc,0) + COALESCE(tablet,0) + COALESCE(phone,0)) AS total_devices
FROM web_devices
accepted.description: Canonical daily device counts with a derived total column. Use for device-share calculations and joining to other daily web metrics. | Use for: device share per day; trend of overall device counts; join devices to web demographics or page visits by day

accepted.name: web_demographics_unpivot
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT day, 'M' AS gender_letter, 'tw' AS channel_shortcut, m_tw_cnt AS measure_cnt, m_tw_qty AS measure_qty FROM web_demographics
UNION ALL
SELECT day, 'M' AS gender_letter, 'fb' AS channel_shortcut, m_fb_cnt AS measure_cnt, m_fb_qty AS measure_qty FROM web_demographics
UNION ALL
SELECT day, 'F' AS gender_letter, 'tw' AS channel_shortcut, f_tw_cnt AS measure_cnt, f_tw_qty AS measure_qty FROM web_demographics
UNION ALL
SELECT day, 'F' AS gender_letter, 'fb' AS channel_shortcut, f_fb_cnt AS measure_cnt, f_fb_qty AS measure_qty FROM web_demographics
accepted.description: Unpivots daily web demographics into one row per day x gender x channel x measure (cnt vs qty). Useful for flexible aggregations and joins to channel/gender dimensions. | Use for: compare channels by gender; time series of counts vs quantities per segment; join to channels_dim or gender_dim for labels

accepted.name: orders_latest_by_customer
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.id AS id,
  o.customer_id AS customer_id,
  o.ordered AS ordered,
  o.delivery AS delivery,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY o.customer_id ORDER BY o.ordered DESC) AS rn_order_by_customer
FROM orders o
accepted.description: Most recent order per customer with order metadata. Exposes a row_number rank so callers can select the latest or top-N orders per customer. | Use for: latest order for each customer; recent order cohorts; top-N recent orders per customer

accepted.name: picking_activity_window
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  pl.picklist_id AS picklist_id,
  pl.log_time AS log_time,
  pl.activity AS activity,
  pl.location_id AS location_id,
  pl.pickline_no AS pickline_no,
  LAG(pl.log_time) OVER (PARTITION BY pl.picklist_id ORDER BY pl.log_time) AS prev_log_time,
  LEAD(pl.log_time) OVER (PARTITION BY pl.picklist_id ORDER BY pl.log_time) AS next_log_time,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY pl.picklist_id ORDER BY pl.log_time) AS seq_in_picklist,
  COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY pl.picklist_id) AS total_events_in_picklist
FROM picking_log pl
accepted.description: Ordered picking_log events per picklist with lag/lead and a running count. Useful for analyzing picklist workflows, durations between activities, and sequence patterns. | Use for: time between pick events; sequence analysis of picking activities; identify first/last activity per picklist

accepted.name: employee_supervision_paths
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT id AS emp_id, name AS name, supervisor_id AS supervisor_id, 0 AS depth, CAST(id AS TEXT) AS path_ids
FROM employees
WHERE supervisor_id IS NULL
UNION ALL
SELECT e.id AS emp_id, e.name AS name, e.supervisor_id AS supervisor_id, esp.depth + 1 AS depth, esp.path_ids || '>' || CAST(e.id AS TEXT) AS path_ids
FROM employees e
JOIN employee_supervision_paths esp ON e.supervisor_id = esp.emp_id
accepted.description: Recursive hierarchy of employee -> supervisor paths. Produces one row per employee-ancestor pair with depth. Useful for org-chart traversals and reporting up the management chain. | Use for: reporting chain for an employee; compute levels between employees and supervisors; build full org paths for visualization

accepted.name: product_reorder_guidance
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.id AS id,
  p.name AS name,
  COALESCE(SUM(i.qty),0) AS available_qty,
  pm.qty_minimum AS qty_minimum,
  pm.qty_purchase AS qty_purchase
FROM products p
LEFT JOIN inventory i ON p.id = i.product_id
LEFT JOIN product_minimums pm ON p.id = pm.product_id
GROUP BY p.id, p.name, pm.qty_minimum, pm.qty_purchase
accepted.description: Per-product current inventory quantity and minimum/purchase rules to support reorder decisions. Exposes aggregated available_qty and compares to qty_minimum and qty_purchase. Use as input to reorder alerts and recommended purchase sizes. | Use for: which products need reorder; compute reorder quantity based on minimums; join reorder guidance to suppliers or purchases
